summary: Vanuatu waives visas for citizens of the 121 countries and territories on the Department of Immigration and Passport Services' exemption list (as of 8 October 2026) — including the whole EU, the UK, US, Australia, New Zealand, China, India and its Pacific neighbors — for stays of up to 120 days, while everyone else applies in advance, either for a visitor visa valid for up to 30 days or for a tourist visa of up to 120 days.

vaccinations.text: Malaria is transmitted in Vanuatu, mainly P. vivax, and the CDC recommends that travellers take prescription medicine to prevent malaria and talk to their doctor about which medication to take.

source.name: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Vanuatu traveler health

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for Vanuatu. The UK Foreign Office advises having travel insurance that covers local treatment and unexpected medical evacuation.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Vanuatu travel advice (health)

onwardTicket.text: The Department of Immigration lists a return airline ticket, and a confirmed accommodation or local address, among the documents non-citizens must produce on arrival.

source.name: One Way Ticket Info – Department of Immigration and Passport Services

proofOfFunds.text: Visitor visa applicants must show funds or income of at least 40,000 vatu for each month of the stay, or evidence of support from family or friends in Vanuatu. No sum is published for visa-exempt visitors.

source.name: Visit Vanuatu – visitor visa, Department of Immigration and Passport Services

currencyLimits.text: No official source we could read states Vanuatu's cash-declaration threshold.

notes: The UK FCDO says possession of even small quantities of drugs can lead to imprisonment and a large fine.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says the risk of crime is generally low, but there have been burglaries accompanied by violence and some street crime and attacks on foreign nationals, including tourists at nightclubs and bars in Port Vila. It says Vanuatu is in an active seismic region where volcanic eruptions, earthquakes and tsunamis are possible, and that the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May.

tips.text: The EU suspended its visa-waiver agreement with Vanuatu in whole over Vanuatu's investor citizenship schemes (Council Decision (EU) 2022/2198), and EU Regulation 2018/1806 lists Vanuatu among the nationalities that need a visa. Vanuatu's Department of Immigration still lists every EU state as visa-exempt.

The UK FCDO says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to May, though cyclones can happen at any time of year, bringing strong winds, heavy rain, flooding, landslides and road closures.

The UK FCDO lists active volcanoes on Ambae, Ambrym, Epi, Gaua, Lopevi, Tanna and Vanua Lava, and says alert levels can change unexpectedly and may stop access to an island. Check current levels with the Vanuatu Meteorology and Geo-hazards Department and the latest advice with the Vanuatu Tourism Office before you go.

The UK FCDO says local customs are strictly observed and should be respected, that beachwear should not be worn away from beaches and hotels, and that some kava bars (nakamals), particularly outside Port Vila, do not welcome women. It also says to always ask permission before photographing people.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Vanuatu?
faq.answer: Most travelers do not. Citizens of all EU states, the UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, China, Japan, India, South Africa, most Gulf states and Vanuatu's Pacific neighbors are visa-exempt for stays of up to 120 days. Nationalities not on the exemption list apply before traveling, either for a visitor visa valid for up to 30 days (7,420 VUV) or for a non-extendable tourist visa of up to 120 days (5,150 VUV).

faq.question: How long can I stay in Vanuatu without a visa?
faq.answer: Up to 120 days for visa-exempt nationalities, granted on arrival as a tourist visa. The Department of Immigration says it cannot be extended and you must leave before the 120 days expire.

faq.question: Has the EU suspended visa-free travel with Vanuatu?
faq.answer: Yes. The EU suspended its short-stay visa-waiver agreement with Vanuatu in whole over Vanuatu's investor citizenship schemes (Council Decision (EU) 2022/2198), and EU Regulation 2018/1806 lists Vanuatu among the nationalities that need a visa for the Schengen area. Vanuatu's Department of Immigration still lists every EU state as visa-exempt.

faq.question: How does the Vanuatu e-Visa work?
faq.answer: Travelers from countries outside the exemption list apply online to the Department of Immigration before departure, with a certified passport copy, a return ticket, and evidence of funds (at least 40,000 vatu a month) or of support from family or friends in Vanuatu. No processing time is published.

faq.question: What will I be asked for on arrival?
faq.answer: A passport valid for more than 6 months on the date you arrive and a confirmed onward or return ticket. Visitor-visa applicants must also show funds of at least 40,000 vatu for each month of the stay, or support from family or friends in Vanuatu; no amount is published for visa-exempt visitors.
